value: This article addresses the common neurological sequelae of COVID-19, focusing on "brain fog" experienced by an estimated 22-32% of recovered patients as part of long COVID or PASC. It details how this cognitive impairment affects attention, memory, and executive function, noting its prevalence even in non-hospitalized and mild cases. Furthermore, it highlights a German study demonstrating that even young individuals with mild COVID, who reported no cognitive issues, exhibited measurable deficits in attention and memory. While acknowledging study limitations, the article suggests these cognitive effects of COVID-19 may be more widespread than previously thought but also potentially reversible, with observed improvements in memory and attention within six to nine months post-infection.
